beta_new: A juggy shallow dihedral with a crack, ten feet left of Aqualung, begins the route. Blast easy ground to the lofty first bolt, pass the roof on its left, then trend rightward up the steep wall, through small bulges, to the anchors.
Begin beside the low roof's right extremity, head diagonally left into a short dihedral, then pass three small bulges to the anchors.
Begin a short distance right of the preceding route and rocket up a juggy wall through overhangs, clipping eight bolts to the anchors.

First reach the anchored shelf that ends the second Conn's East pitch, using any earlier route. From just left of those anchors, jam the gorgeous cracks in the orange rock up to a ceiling, pull over it, and finish on easier ground.
Follow eight bolts up the center of the wall, passing flakes that face left, to the anchors beneath a roof.
Begin at the right edge of a triangular low roof, work leftward and upward along a slanting ramp to a rest, then finish the nice face with two bolts.
Start on the shelf's right half and take the right-hand bolt line, six bolts, to the anchors.
Start a dozen feet beyond the previous route and power up flakes and huecos, clipping four bolts, until a slot where small cams go, then cut left to the anchors.
Start inside the dihedral that sits left of the bolts and climb it to a small ledge before taking on the bolted wall.
Start next to a twenty-five-foot boulder, on its left, and climb the orange wall, clipping eight bolts to the anchors.
Climb a shallow corner into the roof, shift about six feet leftward to pull it, then finish with a few further tough moves up to the anchors.
A crack gets you started, a bolt marks the rightward step onto a horizontal break, then you shuffle left briefly before heading straight up the wall to a ledge under the summit roof.
Follow the corner crack, pull the small roof, then take the finger crack above to the top; a tree with slings serves as the lower-off.
Begin at a brief vertical crack, then track the bolts up the orange fissure and past the overhang's left flank to the anchors.
Follow the leaning crack up to an anchor, then rappel or keep going and finish via the second pitch of Unrelenting Verticality.

Start by the right-facing corner and work into the orange corner above, then step right across a bulge onto a good shelf. After lunch, go left through a second bulge to the thin final moves, eight bolts in all.
Stand on the big belay block, stick-clipping bolt one, and latch flaky, slanting holds. The featured face above has eight more bolts leading to the anchors.

moves.from: The featured face above has eight more bolts leading to the anchors.

beta_new: Launch from beneath the roof's midpoint and muscle up the bulging wall's center, clipping seven bolts.
A flake that fades out beneath the roof starts the route; send the roof, power past seven bolts, then finish the arete with three more bolts.

moves.from: power past seven bolts, then finish the arete with three more bolts

beta_new: Climb Old Testament to its anchors, then drop down and right and keep traversing the entire roof to a second set of anchors, nineteen bolts overall.
Start fifteen feet beyond the big belay block, take the wall and flaring corner, then finish up the high arete, clipping eleven bolts.
Step off a big block beneath the sharp arete and send it, clipping ten bolts to the anchors.
Start adjacent to a large corner and crank up the abundant buckets past eight bolts to the anchors.
Begin on jugs under a small overhang at the cirque's left side, pull through it and across a smooth wall to a ledge, then continue through some bulges to the anchors.
Climb Reaches from Hell up to bolt three, then trend rightward with the bolts across a roof of jugs to the cold shuts.
Step off a block and head out right to bolt one, then work up the steep wall past eight more bolts to the anchors.

moves.from: past eight more bolts to the anchors

beta_new: Start on the face's left half and climb the first two bolts to the low shelf, then continue up the wall above, past four more bolts to the anchors.

moves.from: climb the first two bolts to the low shelf, then continue up the wall above, past four more bolts to the anchors

beta_new: A little inside corner opens the route, small cracks take you across a bulge, then the line drifts a touch leftward to the anchors.
The wall leans back slightly, and a succession of flakes carries you up to anchors beneath a huge roof.
The crux first pitch starts from a block and clips five bolts to a hanging belay. The second pitch fires through eight more bolts up to the summit at an easier grade.

moves.from: The crux first pitch starts from a block and clips five bolts to a hanging belay. The second pitch fires through eight more bolts up to the summit at an easier grade.

beta_new: Begin next to the Biohazard crack-and-corner, on its left, and follow seven bolts to the anchors.
Haul yourself up the orange rock along its central line to the anchors.
Ascend the arete bordering the cave's right side as far as bolt one, then veer left and stride up the steep wall, which has five further bolts, to the anchors.
Tiny edges and cracks lead to a bolt midway, a bulge gives access to a white wall, and you finish by angling up-left onto the Ecstasy Junior crack.

Two hard pitches. The first begins in a small corner under a low ceiling and follows five bolts up to a ledge with anchors; the second starts twenty feet right of those anchors and climbs six more bolts, finishing beneath the top of the cliff.

Starting at the anchors beside the tree, on the big ledge's right, hand-traverse the horizontal flake rightward to the Crescendo anchors, clipping the sport routes' lowest bolts where you can. Placing the rope on the far side of the flake protects both leader and second.

Work up a shallow flake angled to the right, then continue on the wall, clipping two bolts that are strenuous to reach, and follow a seam up to an overhang. Swing around it on the left to reach the anchors on Conn's East.
Begin in a small dihedral next to a horizontal crack with good holds, climb the corner, shuffle out along the crack by hand, then climb the blunt white arete, eight bolts in all.
Six bolts mark the way, starting a few feet to the right of an inside corner.
Seven bolts protect the wall above a starting crack that sits right of the vegetated corner.
